sections.title: A solution to Haagerup's problem: Normality of weights is commutatively determined
themes: Functional analysis & operator algebras (added theme; no controlled theme precisely fits)
sections.abstract: The authors show that lower semi-continuity of a weight on a C*-algebra, and normality of a weight on a von Neumann algebra, can each be detected by restricting the corresponding property to commutative subalgebras.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that a weight is lower semi-continuous if it is so on commutative C*-subalgebras, and derive the von Neumann analogue that commutative testing detects normality—affirmatively resolving Haagerup's second problem on normal weights.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Weights on C*-algebras and von Neumann algebras; the tests concern all relevant commutative subalgebras and positive sums, with normality for von Neumann algebra weights understood in the usual directed-supremum sense.
sections.unique_caveat: This is specifically the second of Haagerup's problems on normal weights; it is not a general solution to unrelated operator-algebra problems.
sections.ranking_evidence: A precise answer to a named problem posed by Haagerup in 1975, with a second functional-analysis category; the introduction states explicit equivalences for both C*-algebras and von Neumann algebras.

sections.title: Operator limits of random matrices: Edge universality and sharp approximations
sections.abstract: For Wigner matrices, the authors prove convergence of rescaled Lanczos operators at the spectral edge to the stochastic Airy operator, and construct sharp operator couplings for several classical random-matrix ensembles.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves convergence in distribution of embedded resolvents for general Wigner matrices to the stochastic Airy operator and reports sharp couplings to stochastic Airy, Bessel, and Sine operators for Gaussian, Laguerre, and circular β-ensembles, respectively.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The Wigner theorem uses independent real-symmetric or complex-Hermitian entries, the Lee–Yin off-diagonal tail condition, and uniform integrability of standardized diagonal squares; the limit is at the upper spectral edge with deterministic starting vectors. The coupling results concern the specified classical ensembles.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper uses the Lee–Yin tail condition as a sufficient hypothesis and explicitly does not establish that it is necessary for operator convergence in the topology considered.
sections.ranking_evidence: Crosses probability, mathematical physics, and numerical analysis; its introduction states operator-norm resolvent convergence and joint spectral consequences, while the abstract gives explicit approximation rates for three operator limits.

sections.title: Improved lattice-packing bounds in small dimensions
sections.abstract: The author modifies the Cohn–Elkies linear program using restrictions on short lattice vectors to improve upper bounds for lattice-packing density in a range of dimensions.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves a modified linear-programming upper bound, based on constraints on how short vectors can occur in residue classes modulo 2; the reported bounds improve the cited comparisons in the dimensions listed in the abstract.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Full-rank lattices in Euclidean n-space, normalized to have minimum nonzero vector length 1; the bound is for lattice packing density, not unrestricted sphere packings.
sections.unique_caveat: The author says the improvement diminishes as dimension grows and that the modified and standard programs become equivalent for sufficiently large dimensions; further class-counting refinements are omitted.
sections.ranking_evidence: It improves on the three-point bound in dimensions 11–16 and reports values below published numerical Cohn–Elkies bounds in additional dimension ranges; the paper supplies exact rational certificates and links numerical data.
sections.comment: Links to a GitHub repository with relevant numerical data

sections.title: Parabolic Rectifiable Reifenberg for Measures
sections.abstract: The author announces a parabolic structure theory for Radon measures, including rectifiability criteria via Jones square functions and sharp results for Lp beta numbers in space-time.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims a parabolic rectifiable Reifenberg theorem for arbitrary Radon measures, qualitative and quantitative characterizations of regular parabolic rectifiability using Jones square functions, and sharp Lp beta-number results in every parabolic dimension.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Measures on R^n × R with parabolic distance; the abstract describes arbitrary Radon measures and all parabolic dimensions, but does not give the full theorem hypotheses or constants.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract presents the work as an announcement; applications of the characterizations require checking the paper's complete hypotheses and definitions. The formalization is reported by the author and was not independently audited here.
sections.ranking_evidence: Three mathematical categories are represented, and the abstract claims an extension of several established rectifiability theories to parabolic space-time; the author reports a Lean 4/Mathlib formalization of the stated results and proofs.
sections.comment: Comments are welcome. 15 pages, 7 figures, link to a GitHub repository for formalization

sections.title: Complete entropy contraction from conditional hyperboundedness
themes: Functional analysis & operator algebras (added theme; no controlled theme precisely fits)
sections.abstract: For finite-dimensional quantum channels, the authors derive relative-entropy contraction from conditional hyperboundedness and strict GNS contraction, including an explicit modified logarithmic Sobolev lower bound for KMS-symmetric quantum Markov semigroups.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove relative entropy contraction under the stated channel hypotheses and, for KMS-symmetric semigroups, give α = λ(1−2/q) / [12(λt₀ + log M + 1−2/q)] under conditional 2-to-q hyperboundedness at t₀ and GNS gap λ.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite-dimensional quantum channels compatible with a faithful conditional expectation; the semigroup result assumes KMS symmetry, conditional hyperboundedness with constant M at t₀ > 0, q > 2, and a positive GNS gap λ.
sections.unique_caveat: The bound is conditional on both smoothing and gap inputs; the abstract does not claim the constant is optimal or that the hypotheses are necessary.
sections.ranking_evidence: Cross-listed in functional analysis and operator algebras; the abstract supplies an explicit constant linking a GNS gap and a conditional 2-to-q hyperboundedness estimate, plus a complete version for auxiliary systems.

sections.title: Properties C and D fail for C_n^r whenever n ≡ 2 mod 4, n ≥ 6 and r ≥ 4
sections.abstract: For finite abelian groups C_n^r in the stated range, the author constructs zero-sum-free sequences showing that Properties C and D fail and obtains a lower bound for the Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv constant.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves that Properties C and D fail throughout that range and gives s(C_n^r) ≥ 2^r(n−1) + 2^(r−2) + 1 for the Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv constant.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Sequences over the finite abelian group C_n^r; the theorem requires n ≡ 2 (mod 4), n ≥ 6, and r ≥ 4. Here s(C_n^r) concerns zero-sum subsequences of length exactly n.
sections.unique_caveat: The result supplies lower bounds and failures of the structural properties, not exact values of the zero-sum constants throughout the range.
sections.ranking_evidence: A parameterized counterexample, rather than an isolated small case, overturns both conjectured structural properties for every n ≡ 2 mod 4 with n ≥ 6 and rank r ≥ 4; it links additive number theory with combinatorics.

sections.title: Stable homotopy theory of higher categories with adjoints
sections.abstract: The author develops homotopy invariants for (∞,∞)-categories with adjoints, proves a Whitehead theorem and long oriented exact sequences, and relates categorical spectra with adjoints to categorical chain complexes.
sections.claimed_result: The author defines homotopy monoidal categories from iterated endomorphisms, recovers homotopy groups of the classifying space, proves a Whitehead theorem and long oriented exact sequences, and establishes an equivalence between skeletal sequences of categorical spectra with adjoints and categorical chain complexes.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Based at a point of an (∞,∞)-category with adjoints; the proposed invariants are monoidal categories with duals, replacing iterated loop spaces by iterated endomorphisms.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract's claim that this theory is at least as rich as classical homotopy theory is not a claim of equivalence with all classical homotopy types; its theorems apply in the specified higher-categorical setting.
sections.ranking_evidence: The paper claims several concrete structural results—recovery of classical homotopy groups, a Whitehead theorem, exact sequences, and a homological-algebra equivalence—within a new categorical setting.
